programme.title: Angie Gensler
programme.desc: News - Angie Gensler is a mother and personal trainer who was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2004. In this episode, Mathew Embry speaks with Angie about her diagnosis and why she ultimately chose not to pursue drug treatments. Instead, she focused on lifestyle changes including diet, exercise, and daily discipline. Along the way she faced several major challenges including a serious car accident, a hysterectomy, and the effects of menopause, all while continuing to pursue optimal health and eventually stepping onto the competitive bodybuilding stage in her 50s. Her story is an inspiration to anyone navigating a difficult diagnosis.

programme.title: Trevor Wicken
programme.desc: News - Movement may be one of the most powerful tools available for people living with multiple sclerosis. In this episode of Hope & Health, Mathew Embry speaks with Trevor Wicken, founder of The MS Gym, about how targeted movement training can help people with MS improve mobility, strength, and neurological function. The conversation explores neuroplasticity, foot drop, and the discipline required to stay consistent with movement when living with a neurological condition. Trevor also shares how a spinal injury at 16 shaped his philosophy and how two women living with MS ultimately changed the direction of his career and led to the creation of The MS Gym

programme.desc: News - Movement may be one of the most powerful tools available for people living with multiple sclerosis. In this episode of Hope & Health, Mathew Embry speaks with Trevor Wicken, founder of The MS Gym, about how targeted movement training can help people with MS improve mobility, strength, and neurological function. The conversation explores neuroplasticity, foot drop, and the discipline required to stay consistent with movement when living with a neurological condition. programme.desc: Amanda is an avid art collector and curator, but her Mid-Century home in Ormond was becoming small, and the need for more space for both her art and family was paramount. programme.sub-title: This Mid-Century Home Has Been Simply Updated for an Art Lover

programme.desc: Can You Believe This Headboard is ALL plywood??? Time to get building! This bed was inspired by the horizontal slat design I incorporated in my recent TV console Build! Material isn't cheap right now and this is a great way of utilizing edge banding and plywood for a premium look! Thanks for watching!
programme.sub-title: DIY "All-Plywood" Mid Century Modern Platform Bed

programme.title: Bold Backyards
programme.desc: This DIY raised planter is fully made out of cinder blocks! These blocks are staked and then filled with dirt and rock. If I were in a more wet area, I would have installed a drain, we are in a pretty dry area, and this dirt is mostly granite, clay, and rock. I have found there isn't much settling that occurs in this area.

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: It's fall and there are mountains of leaves around our yards. But this abundance of leaves can be put to great use around the landscape. Consider shredding your leaves to create a nutrient-rich ground cover for your yard and planting beds.

programme.desc: From urban eco-living and reimagined sports venues to modern libraries and heritage restorations, this episode celebrates design shaping how we live, play, and connect.

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: The need for a new development model is desperately needed, a model which is sustainable and financially accessible with a focus on townhouses in urban locations. HYPE teaming up with architect Chris Gilbert from Archier to design, build and develop three sustainable townhouses in Brunswick. Oh did we mention they also live here?

programme.desc: Welcome to the Passive House Ranch! Homeowners Beate and Bern have created a state of the art modern home while preserving the structure's original character. Their passive house has a classic ranch design with high-performance features that bring next-level comfort.

programme.title: Rise: Sustainable Home Tours
programme.desc: Passive House is an easy to understand building standard that takes home energy efficiency to a whole new level using 5 building standards that are explained in this video.

programme.title: Rise: Sustainable Home Tours

Subtle interventions were made during the heritage renovation, including the inclusion of a glass lift, but all was done to not only honour its past but also reflect how we live today.
programme.sub-title: Keeping the Heritage Alive in this 1880s Home Renovation

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: Bold Backyards
programme.desc: This DIY raised planter is fully made out of cinder blocks! These blocks are staked and then filled with dirt and rock. Traditionally you would pour a concrete footing and then stack the block; I wanted to see if it would work with rock and block adhesive. I love how it turned out, and it's doing amazing so far. If I were in a more wet area, I would have installed a drain, we are in a pretty dry area, and this dirt is mostly granite, clay, and rock. I have found there isn't much settling that occurs in this area.

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

In this video, we'll show you shipping container homes and building examples from around the world and ask whether or not shipping container construction is the future?
The tiny house movement is growing rapidly and more container buildings are being constructed around the world, but is this the future of sustainable architecture? In this video, we visit a range of shipping container projects, such as Buck Street market and Container City in London, in order to investigate the legibility for growth in the future.
Some people think these buildings are a ‘scam’ while others think they are the future, so let's find out.

programme.title: Bold Backyards
programme.desc: This DIY raised planter is fully made out of cinder blocks! These blocks are staked and then filled with dirt and rock. Traditionally you would pour a concrete footing and then stack the block; I wanted to see if it would work with rock and block adhesive. I love how it turned out, and it's doing amazing so far. If I were in a more wet area, I would have installed a drain, we are in a pretty dry area, and this dirt is mostly granite, clay, and rock. I have found there isn't much settling that occurs in this area.
